text_blocks.snippet: Cerebrovascular disease, which includes stroke, arises from disruptions to blood flow in the brain, often due to blockages or ruptures of blood vessels. Common causes include blood clots (thrombosis or embolism), blood vessel narrowing (atherosclerosis), and vessel ruptures (hemorrhage). Risk factors for cerebrovascular disease include high blood pressure, smoking, high cholesterol, diabetes, and a sedentary lifestyle.
